branches: Yes: document the call in the patient record and close the alert with the close time
No after 3 attempts: let the provider know; provider decides on a police welfare check or a letter; mark the alert open, pt not reached, and hand it off verbally to the next triage nurse

answer.explanation: When a critical lab alert comes in, the first thing is to write down the pickup time, since the one-hour window started when the lab flagged it, not when the alert was opened. The result is then matched to the patient by name and date of birth. If either one does not line up, the lab gets called back and no provider is paged until the result is confirmed. Once it is confirmed, the ordering provider is paged, and if they do not call back in 15 minutes the page goes out again. If there is still no answer 15 minutes after that second page, the on-call provider for the day gets called, and if they cannot be reached either, the medical director's cell is the last option. Every page attempt is logged with a time. When a provider finally calls back, the value is read back to them word for word and they confirm it, and their name, the time, and the read back confirmation go into the result entry. The provider then decides whether the patient goes to the ED right away or can wait. For the ED route, the patient is called and told to go to the nearest ED, and the ED charge nurse at Riverside General gets a quick handoff. For a non-urgent route, the patient gets exact instructions, and a repeat lab gets ordered with our draw hours given. Patient calls go to the primary number first, then the alternate, with a callback message that does not reveal results if nobody answers, and up to three tries over about an hour. Once the patient has the instructions and the call is documented, the alert is closed with the time. If the patient cannot be reached after three tries, the provider decides whether to request a welfare check or send a letter, and the alert stays open and is handed to the next triage nurse.
trace_answers: Scenario a: After neither page gets an answer, the on-call provider is contacted once the 15-minute wait after the second page runs out. The on-call provider calls back and says the patient needs the ED. Read the value back to them word for word, get their confirmation, and document their name, the time, and read back confirmed. Then call the patient on the first try, tell them to go to the nearest ED, and call the Riverside General ED charge nurse with a handoff covering the patient name, date of birth, the value, and the ordering provider. Document the patient call in the patient record, noting what was said and that the patient understood, and close the alert in the critical log with the close time. The page attempts to the ordering provider stay logged with their times.

Scenario b: The provider's repeat lab order for tomorrow cannot be completed with the patient because they were never reached, so the draw hours and instructions are not passed along. After the third failed call attempt, the provider is told the patient was not reached and decides on a police welfare check or a letter. The alert is not closed. It gets marked open, pt not reached in the critical log and handed off verbally to the next triage nurse.

For URGENT referrals, call the patient the same day and book into the held urgent slots so the visit happens within 7 days
For ROUTINE referrals, book the next available new-patient slot by phone, or by portal message if the patient uses the portal
Make up to 3 scheduling attempts on different days; for urgent referrals complete all 3 within 2 days and tell the triage nurse after the 2nd miss
If the patient cannot be reached after 3 attempts, mail the Unable to Reach letter, notify the referring office, and set status CLOSED-NO-CONTACT
Once booked, send the appointment confirmation to the referring office and the new-patient packet (forms, medication list sheet, directions) to the patient, then set status SCHEDULED

answer.explanation: New referrals arrive through the e-referral portal and the fax inbox and are checked at least twice a day. Each one is logged in the tracker right away because the days-open count starts there. The packet is then checked for required items, and if anything is missing the referring office is asked for it, with a follow-up call and a closure if nothing arrives within about five business days total. Complete packets go through eligibility, and plans that require prior authorization get an auth request with the office note, while a denial closes the referral and sends the decision back to the referring office. Regardless of auth status, the triage nurse reviews the referral and marks it urgent or routine, which sets how fast the patient is called and booked. Once an appointment is confirmed, the referring office and the patient both get their paperwork and the referral is marked scheduled. Referrals that cannot be reached or completed are closed with letters so nothing stays open indefinitely.
trace_answers: If the referral arrives without insurance information and the referring office does not respond, the referral is set to HOLD-INFO and the office is sent the Incomplete Referral request. After 3 business days with no answer, a second request goes out and the referral coordinator is called. If there is still nothing 2 business days after that, the referral is set to CLOSED-INCOMPLETE and a closure letter is faxed to the referring provider.

If a complete referral is for an HMO patient whose plan requires prior auth and the triage nurse marks it URGENT, the auth request is submitted with the office note and set to AUTH-PENDING, and because the referral is urgent, expedited review is requested. Triage happens while auth is pending. The patient is called the same day and all 3 attempts are made within 2 days, with the triage nurse told after the 2nd miss. The patient can only be booked once auth is approved, so it is booked into a held urgent slot within 7 days of approval, then the confirmation goes to the referring office and the new-patient packet goes to the patient and the referral is set to SCHEDULED. If auth is denied, scheduling stops and the referral is closed as CLOSED-DENIED.
